title: Which pins does the band touch?
hook: A rubber band round 10 pins. One walk, left turns kept, right turns dropped, finds it.

knows: left and right turns (shown on the stage as keep and drop)
doesNotKnow: how a program finds the outline around a set of points
that checking left or right turn for three points is all the geometry needed

misconception: The outline of a cloud of points is just its leftmost, rightmost, top and bottom points.
objective: The learner can explain that the band corners are wherever the boundary turns, found by sorting the pins once and dropping any pin that makes a right turn, so some corners are not extreme pins and some inside pins are dropped.

claims.source: Builder's node script: Andrew's monotone chain gives (-1,4) (0,0) (6,1) (8,3) (7,7) (2,8); the Graham scan walk used on the stage gives the same set. The brief used (6,0); the spec moved it to (6,1) so the extremes are unambiguous (brief fix applied).

claims.text: The leftmost, rightmost, top and bottom pins are 4 of the 6 band pins: (-1,4), (8,3), (2,8) and (0,0). Pins 1 and 6 in the stage's order, (6,1) and (7,7), are on the band but are none of them.
claims.source: Builder's node script: extremes of x and y over the 10 pins are 4 distinct pins; the other 2 hull pins are (6,1) and (7,7). Order numbers are the angle order from (0,0).

claims.text: Walking the pins in angle order from the lowest pin and dropping the previous corner on each right turn drops exactly 4 pins, (5,2), (2,2), (3,3) and (4,5), each at a right turn, and ends on the 6 band pins.
claims.source: Builder's node trace of the scan used in Demo.tsx: cross products -3, -5, -20, -13 (all strictly right turns, never a straight line), one drop at most per tap; the other 5 pins are never dropped. Ties in angle sort nearer first and pop on cross <= 0. (2,2) and (3,3) share an angle from (0,0); they are tapped nearer first. The spec said no two pins share an angle; the sort handles it.

claims.text: Sorting the pins round the start once and then making one pass of left-or-right checks is Graham's scan, which takes about n log n steps for n pins.
claims.source: Graham (1972), An efficient algorithm for determining the convex hull of a finite planar set, Information Processing Letters 1(4); CLRS 3rd ed. section 33.3 (Graham's scan, O(n lg n)). CLRS 4th ed. dropped the computational geometry chapter, so no works.json entry exists.

claims.text: A turn at three points is a right turn when the cross product of the two steps is negative.
claims.source: CLRS 3rd ed. section 33.1 (direction by cross product). Used in Demo.tsx as cross(o, a, b) <= 0 means drop.

recall.question: Pins sorted round the lowest one, and you add the next pin. When do you drop the previous corner?
options: When the three points make a right turn
When the new pin is higher
When the previous corner is nearest the start
recall.why: A right turn at the previous corner means it lies inside the band through its neighbours, so the band cannot touch it.
